# Gate G1: alignment

**Tile:** Fargo, ND — lat 46.88, lon -96.79, extent 1000 m, EPSG:32614.
**Generated by:** `tools/g1_overlays.py <cache> <out>` (gate tooling; nothing in the
pipeline depends on it).

Every layer is resampled onto **one common 1 m grid** covering the intersection of the
four cached rasters (1120 x 1120 px), so a misalignment would show up as a visible
offset instead of being hidden by the layers' differing native resolutions.

| PNG | Content |
|---|---|
| `01_hillshade_buildings.png` | GEDTM30 hillshade, building outlines in red |
| `02_landcover_buildings.png` | WorldCover palette, building outlines in white |
| `03_chm_v2_buildings.png` | Canopy v2 (black -> green ramp), outlines in red |
| `04_chm_v1_buildings.png` | Canopy v1, same scale |
| `05_panel.png` | All four on one 2x2 sheet, same grid and scale |

## Quantitative agreement

The pictures are backed by numbers, because "looks aligned" is not measurable.

**A. Overture footprints vs WorldCover built-up** (two fully independent sources)

| | |
|---|---|
| building pixels on built-up class | **93.0 %** |
| built-up share of the tile | 85.8 % (chance level) |

The margin over chance is modest only because this tile is overwhelmingly built-up;
see the caveat below.

**B. WorldCover tree mask vs canopy height** (again independent sources)

| | v1 | v2 |
|---|---|---|
| mean height on tree class | 3.89 m | 4.79 m |
| mean height off tree class | 0.43 m | 0.64 m |
| tree pixels taller than 2 m | 40.5 % | 45.1 % |
| non-tree pixels taller than 2 m | 5.0 % | 7.4 % |
| mean height inside building footprints | 0.21 m | 0.29 m |

Canopy is **8x** more likely to exceed 2 m inside the WorldCover tree mask than outside
it. Two sources built from different imagery by different teams agree on where the trees
are.

## What the images show

- **Buildings sit in the street grid**, not across it, in all four layers. Individual
  tree crowns resolve as distinct blobs that fall in the gaps *between* footprints and
  along streets. A systematic offset would put crowns on top of roofs; none does.
- **The canopy map is near-zero inside building footprints** (0.21 / 0.29 m mean). The
  rooftop contamination G3 asks about is small on this tile, so the WorldCover tree mask
  is doing little work here. That is a property of this tile, not a general result.
- **The hillshade shows no rooftop signature at all** — only a smooth drainage feature
  running diagonally. That independently confirms GEDTM30 is true bare earth, which is
  the premise behind SPEC.md's rejection of GLO-30 and SRTM as terrain.

## Caveats, stated rather than buried

1. **This tile is 85.8 % built-up and only 9.0 % tree cover.** It is a good alignment
   target, because buildings are the sharpest features available and there are 795 of
   them, but it is a *poor* canopy tile. G2 and G3 both call for a forested tile, and
   one should be proposed separately rather than reusing this one.
2. **The hillshade is visibly faceted at the 21 m source resolution.** `gdaldem` is
   computing a gradient on a bilinearly upsampled grid, so slope is discontinuous at
   source-cell boundaries. This is an artefact of the gate tooling, not of the cache;
   the terrain builder uses bicubic upsampling (SPEC.md 6.5), which will not do this.
3. The overlays were checked pixelwise, not just by eye: both overlay images contain
   **only** their base colours plus the exact outline colour, so no outline is a
   rendering artefact.

## Bug found and fixed while producing this evidence

Building the common grid exposed that **the cached rasters did not all cover the padded
box.** `gdalwarp` with `-te` and `-tr` rounds the pixel count to *nearest*, so an extent
that is not an exact multiple of the resolution can round **down**:

```
landcover  176x176 @ 6.3518 m  ->  1117.926 m, i.e. 2.074 m short on the east and south
```

The builders would have sampled outside the raster at the tile edge, and M4's "terrain
covers the padded tile with no gaps" would have failed. `fetch_raster()` now snaps the
extent outward to a whole number of pixels anchored at the padded south-west corner (the
local origin) and passes `-ts` so the pixel count is stated outright. Land cover is now
177 x 177 and all four rasters cover the padded box from a common origin.
